item.title: After opening set collapse, ‘Birds defeat Huskies in fifth set to win consolation final
item.description: Consolation brackets present a unique challenge. The ultimate goal is lost. Instead of playing for first, you play for fifth. Motivation has to come from elsewhere. For this UBC team, they found the drive they needed to end the season on a high note, allowing the T-Birds’ graduating all-star, Lucy Borowski, to end her career on a win.

item.title: Cultures come together in SUBA Trio’s concert at the Chan
item.description: The audience hardly touched their chairs as they danced and clapped along to the SUBA trio’s Afro-Cuban-Venezulan jazz-fusion at the Chan Centre.

item.title: Point of Inquiry: Lawyers at AMS council are never a good sign
item.description: The Executive Performance & Accountability Committee is done, for now. Its replacement needs to be more transparent.

item.title: Hackathon coders are the heart of the machine
item.description: Hackathons like cmd-f are as computer science as electric apple pie. Each person, in groups of up to four, attempts to write a functioning computer program in 24 hours. 24 straight hours.

item.title: MUSA mounts musical protest against removal from Chan Centre
item.description: Sidney Shaw / The Ubyssey In early September 2025, students at the UBC School of Music found their access to the Chan Shun Concert Hall severely reduced. MUSA hosted a protest on March 12 featuring performances by musicians from UBC orchestra, choirs, opera, french horn and saxophone quartets, interspersed with speeches from students and alumni.

item.title: MEXSA and the Hatch celebrate International Women’s Day with Purple Thread
item.description: Throughout the week of March 9, the Hatch welcomed Purple Thread, a Women’s Day art exhibition featuring Latin American artists exploring their artistic forms and interpretations of feminism.

item.title: The look-alike contest and the students behind it
item.description: The look-alike contest's appeal could lie in the amusing act of imitation itself, or, more likely, in a desire for community.

item.title: Brave New Play Rites brings the audience to the table read
item.description: Brave New Play Rites features an aspect of the theatre production process that audiences usually don’t get to see: the stage reading.

item.title: From CiTR to Chalamet, Nardwuar will always be a random kid from Vancouver
item.description: When we spoke with Nardwuar the Human Serviette in the CiTR record library, we thought we were on a tight timeline. Nardwuar doesn’t think that way.
